facts.statement: Under the National Recycling Programme, HDB estates get one 660 L blue commingled recycling bin per block, collected at least three times a week (or one 1800/2200 L side-loader bin per block, collected weekly).

Since April 2020 collection from the 660-litre recycling bins at HDB estates was raised from once to at least three times a week; a collector-funded sensor trial that prompts collection at a set fill level was announced for one sector.
facts.source: MSE, written reply to Parliamentary Question on sensors in recycling bins, 4 July 2023

facts.statement: Recyclables collected under the programme are sent to Materials Recovery Facilities for sorting.
facts.source: MSE, written reply to Parliamentary Question on household recycling, 16 February 2021

facts.statement: Singapore's solid-waste disposal infrastructure consists of four waste-to-energy plants, three at Tuas and one at Senoko, plus the offshore Semakau Landfill served by the Tuas Marine Transfer Station.
The domestic recycling rate was 11 per cent in 2025 (overall 52 per cent).
facts.source: NEA, Waste Statistics and Overall Recycling

facts.statement: Domestic waste disposed of in 2025: 1.67 million tonnes.
facts.source: data.gov.sg, Waste Disposed Of And Recycled, Annual (d_72f8e05d45477a7af0c089ad970519da)

facts.statement: 2025: paper/cardboard 1,192,000 t generated, 369,000 t recycled (31 %); plastic 890,000 t generated, 34,000 t recycled (4 %).
facts.source: data.gov.sg, Waste Management And Overall Recycling Rates, Annual (d_daf568968ab40dc81e7b08887a83c8fa)
